title: Named-Project Pipeline — BESS Attach
topic: BESS attach opportunities across the registered named-project web

scope.rationale: Derived on the day by resolving every dossier's relationships[].project against profiler-projects.json: twenty-four dossiers pin the nine registered projects. Tesla is added as the attached supplier of record — its Colossus Megapacks are cited through xAI and its Enbridge Cowboy blocks through Meta rather than pinned by its own relationships[]. The rule, not the list, is the scope: it is re-derived for each edition, and it grew from fifteen companies over eight projects at the 2026-08-30 edition to twenty-five over nine here.

gaps: Named storage suppliers and counterparties that sit outside this scope: ON.energy, Form Energy and Entergy are covered dossiers that pin no registered project, and Jacobs, BorderPlex Digital Assets and Enbridge are not covered at all.
Only two BESS suppliers (Hithium, Tesla) are in scope. This report maps project attach, not supplier rankings — the grid-scale competitive report covers those.

Most scoped companies are private (Crusoe, Vantage, STACK Infrastructure, VoltaGrid, Jupiter Power, xAI and the five general contractors) with no comparable financials; no normalised comparison is attempted.
Oracle is the oldest pin in the set (profileVersion 4, lastUpdated 2026-08-30); its Q1 FY2027 result was expected 2026-09-10 and is not in the record this edition was built from.
Fluidstack is the River Bend lessee and end user but is reached only through Hut 8's and Google's filings; it pins no project of its own.

bluf: Storage is in the plan at four of the nine registered named projects — Lighthouse, Project Jupiter, Stargate Abilene and, on the utility's side of the meter, Hyperion — and a battery supplier is named at none of them [c:c9] [c:c13] [c:c17] [c:c24]. We assess the whitespace this corpus can see is supplier whitespace, not storage whitespace, and that the party to court is the storage-scope holder — the developer, the power-scope contractor or the utility — which is the hyperscaler at only one of the nine [c:c4].

keyJudgments.text: We assess the whitespace across the registered named-project web is supplier whitespace, not storage whitespace. Storage is in the plan at Lighthouse (70% of supply from new solar, wind and battery storage), at Project Jupiter (battery energy storage in the dedicated microgrid), at Stargate Abilene (BESS and solar in the campus power record) and, utility-side, at Hyperion (three grid-scale batteries in the Entergy package) — and no battery supplier is named at any of the four.

We assess four attach lanes are now on the record rather than two: owner-led (Jupiter Power carrying Hithium into Trimount), vendor-led (Tesla riding the operator relationship into Colossus), utility-tolled (a Wyoming utility tolling a 200 MW / 1,600 MWh Tesla battery against Meta's load at Enbridge Cowboy), and developer-fleet (Crusoe contracting ON.energy and Form Energy across campuses rather than for one).

We assess project-level visibility remains the right altitude for BESS business development, and that the map has widened rather than changed shape: twenty-four dossiers now pin nine registered projects against fifteen pinning eight at the last edition, with a new campus (River Bend), a new class of participant (the utility, in AEP and Entergy) and a new tenancy layer (Anthropic on all of Colossus 1) all reached through the same derivation.

We assess the storage-scope holder — not the hyperscaler — is the party to court, and that it differs per campus: Crusoe at Abilene, Vantage with the McCarthy half of the Turner–McCarthy joint venture at Lighthouse, STACK with BorderPlex at Project Jupiter, and Entergy plus Mortenson at Hyperion. Two of those four have delivered utility-scale storage in their own right.

We assess Frontier has moved from the most open of the nine to the least. Its microgrid operator markets the AI-data-centre product line as running with zero reliance on battery storage, holding 40–70% load swings through engine injection, synchronous condensers and flywheels; only the legacy mobile fleet carries a BESS, undisclosed as to supplier, chemistry and capacity.

We assess the owner-led lane that produced Trimount has a covered channel already inside the Stargate programme, in Samsung C&T (a Stargate participant with a Hithium partnership claimed at a 10 GWh pipeline and its own US BESS EPC book) and in Caterpillar (a Colossus and Stargate turbine supplier that sells its own energy-storage blocks). Neither has been reported selling storage into a registered project.

sections.title: What changed since the last edition
sections.read: The corpus movement that made this edition necessary, before any of it is interpreted.
ps: The project web is wider. The 2026-08-30 edition scoped fifteen companies against eight registered projects; the same derivation today resolves twenty-four dossiers against nine. River Bend is the new project — a 245 MW critical-IT campus in West Feliciana Parish, Louisiana, leased for fifteen years to Fluidstack with Google backstopping the USD 7.0 billion base term [c:c28] [c:c30], drawing 330 MW of Entergy capacity from 1 July 2026 with a path to 1,000 MW [c:c29]. Ten participants are new to scope: American Electric Power, Caterpillar, Crusoe, GE Vernova and Samsung C&T at Stargate [c:c34] [c:c38] [c:c39]; Anthropic at Colossus [c:c36]; McCarthy and Whiting-Turner at Lighthouse [c:c21] [c:c23]; Google and Hut 8 at River Bend [c:c28] [c:c30].

Storage moved into the plan at three campuses the last edition recorded as having none. Lighthouse's power commitment is 70% of supply from new zero-emission resources — solar, wind and battery storage — built for the project [c:c9]. Project Jupiter's dedicated on-site microgrid is recorded with battery energy storage alongside the Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells that serve as prime power [c:c13] [c:c15]. And the Stargate flagship at Abilene, whose developer-operator Crusoe entered scope this edition, carries BESS and solar in its Campus 1 power record [c:c24] [c:c27] — with the adjacent Abilene campus Crusoe announced for Microsoft in March 2026 specified as a 900 MW on-site plant plus medium-voltage battery storage [c:c40], which is what the same developer's design language looks like when it is written into an announcement. In none of the three is a battery supplier named at the campus.

A supplier is now named one level up from the campus. Crusoe contracted ON.energy in July 2026 for 5 GW of medium-voltage 'AI UPS' storage across multiple hyperscale campuses [c:c25], and Form Energy in March 2026 for 12 GWh of iron-air capacity from 2027 [c:c26]. The corpus does not assign either to a named building at Abilene — but the developer of the program's flagship campus is buying storage at fleet scale, which is not what a 'None named' cell implied.

Two more lanes surfaced. Meta's clearest battery exposure is Enbridge Cowboy — 365 MW of solar with a 200 MW / 1,600 MWh Tesla battery, tolled through the Wyoming utility rather than sited on a campus [c:c16] — and its Entergy Louisiana package carries three grid-scale batteries with the megawatts undisclosed [c:c17]. Tesla remains in scope as the attached supplier of record without pinning a project of its own: its Colossus position is cited through xAI [c:c4] [c:c5] and its Cowboy blocks through Meta [c:c16].

One prior reading now cuts the other way. VoltaGrid, the microgrid operator at Frontier, advertises its AI-data-centre product line as running with zero reliance on battery storage, holding 40–70% load swings with engine injection, synchronous condensers and flywheels; only its legacy mobile units carry a BESS on the switchgear bus, and its supplier, chemistry and megawatt-hours are undisclosed in every source the corpus holds [c:c12]. Frontier was the last edition's leading whitespace candidate. On the record as it now stands it is the least likely of the nine.

sections.title: Four attach lanes, not two
sections.read: How storage actually got into this web where it did — the sourced route in each case.
ps: **Owner-led.** Jupiter Power signed a 3 GWh supply agreement for Hithium ∞Block containers in June 2024 [c:c3]; the relationship then materialised as Trimount — 2.8 GWh in Everett, Massachusetts, approved by the state siting board in February 2026 with Hithium's 5.015 MWh units confirmed [c:c1] [c:c2]. The supplier never had to win a campus; it won the owner who brings it to one.

**Vendor-led.** Tesla sold $430M of Megapacks to xAI in 2025 [c:c4], and over 240 units now sit at Colossus 1 [c:c5] — the integrator's operator relationship carried the product into the project, and the Megapack 3 / Megablock generation extends the portfolio [c:c6].

**Utility-tolled.** Meta's Enbridge Cowboy pairs 365 MW of solar with a 200 MW / 1,600 MWh Tesla battery that the Wyoming utility tolls, serving Meta data centres without sitting on a Meta campus [c:c16]; the Entergy Louisiana package behind Hyperion carries three more grid-scale batteries with the megawatts undisclosed [c:c17]. The battery is bought by a utility against a hyperscaler's load, not by the hyperscaler.

**Developer-fleet.** Crusoe — the developer-operator of the Stargate flagship at Abilene [c:c24] [c:c27] — contracted ON.energy for 5 GW of medium-voltage AI UPS storage across multiple hyperscale campuses [c:c25] and Form Energy for 12 GWh of iron-air capacity from 2027 [c:c26]. Storage here is procured once, at fleet scale, and allocated to campuses afterwards; nothing in the corpus assigns a block to a named building.

sections.title: Where storage is in the plan and no supplier is named
sections.read: The sourced facts behind the whitespace call, stated at the precision the record supports.
ps: Lighthouse commits 70% of the campus's power to new zero-emission resources built for the project — solar, wind and battery storage — with 30% of that new capacity offered to Wisconsin consumers [c:c9]; the campus is 902 MW of critical IT load and its local approvals remain contested through a referendum and a disputed TIF district [c:c11]. No battery supplier appears anywhere in the record.

Project Jupiter runs a dedicated on-site microgrid recorded with battery energy storage, sized in reporting at 700–900 MW for a first phase against a campus above 1 GW [c:c13], with Bloom solid-oxide fuel cells as the prime-power layer under a master agreement of up to 2.8 GW [c:c15]. No battery supplier is named.

Stargate Abilene lists BESS and solar in its Campus 1 power record beside the grid connection and the on-site plant [c:c24]; the eight buildings topped out in November 2025 [c:c27]. The distinction worth holding is that Crusoe's *other* Abilene campus — the 900 MW build announced for Microsoft in March 2026, outside this project scope — is specified with medium-voltage battery storage in the announcement itself [c:c40]. No battery supplier is named at either, and the two Crusoe has contracted are fleet-level commitments [c:c25] [c:c26].

Hyperion's storage is on the utility's side of the meter: three grid-scale batteries inside the Entergy package that also carries roughly 2.3 GW of approved and 5.2 GW of proposed gas [c:c17]. Megawatts are undisclosed and no supplier is named — the disclosure sits in the Louisiana commission's docket rather than in Meta's own posts.

Homer City and River Bend hold no storage record at all. Homer City is a 4.5 GW gas campus on a retired coal site with Kiewit as EPC [c:c31]; River Bend is grid-served, 330 MW from Entergy on 1 July 2026 against a path to 1,000 MW [c:c29], with Vertiv and Jacobs named as the infrastructure and EPCM partners [c:c28].

sections.title: The Frontier counter-case
sections.read: A prior whitespace candidate that the record now argues against.
ps: Frontier runs off-grid on a 700 MW VoltaGrid natural-gas microgrid built from 210 Jenbacher engines [c:c8]. VoltaGrid's AI-data-centre product line advertises stability without battery storage: 40–70% load swings absorbed through engine high-pressure injection, synchronous condensers and flywheels, and its own control layer, at ±5% voltage and ±2% frequency [c:c12].

Only the legacy mobile fleet carries a BESS, on the switchgear bus for backup and transients, and its supplier, chemistry and megawatt-hours are undisclosed in every source held here [c:c12]. Selling buffering into Frontier means displacing a vendor whose product claim is that buffering is unnecessary.

sections.title: The open lanes — our read
sections.read: Analysis — inference from the sourced facts above, not company statements.
ps: We assess the whitespace this report can see is **supplier** whitespace, not storage whitespace. Storage is in the plan at Lighthouse, Project Jupiter and Stargate Abilene, and on the utility's side of the meter at Hyperion; what is missing at all four is a named battery vendor. The commercial question is therefore not whether these campuses will buy storage but who signs for it — and the record answers that question differently at each one.

We assess the party to court is the storage-scope holder, and it is the hyperscaler at only one of the nine projects. At Abilene it is Crusoe, already buying at fleet scale. At Lighthouse it is Vantage and, practically, the McCarthy half of the Turner–McCarthy joint venture — the one contractor on that campus with a utility-scale storage practice of its own. At Hyperion it is Entergy for the tolled batteries and Mortenson for anything behind the meter. At Project Jupiter it is STACK with BorderPlex. Selling to the hyperscaler at these campuses reaches the party least likely to specify the equipment.

We assess Frontier is now the hardest of the nine rather than the most open. Displacing a vendor whose AI-data-centre product is marketed as needing no battery storage is a different sale from filling an unspecified gap, and nothing in the record suggests VoltaGrid's position there is contested.

We assess the owner-led template that produced Trimount already has a covered channel partner inside the Stargate programme. Samsung C&T is a Stargate participant through the floating-data-centre work and separately holds a global partnership with Hithium claimed at a 10 GWh pipeline, alongside its own US BESS EPC book — the combination that carried Chinese cells into a US project through an owner rather than through a campus. Caterpillar is the second such position: a Colossus and Stargate turbine supplier that also sells its own energy-storage blocks and pairs them with fast-response gen-sets.

We assess the indicator that matters most is no longer 'the first named BESS award at a Stargate campus' but the narrower question of whether ON.energy's or Form Energy's capacity is publicly assigned to Abilene. A fleet-level contract that never resolves to a named campus leaves the attach map exactly where the last edition left it; an assignment converts the developer-fleet lane from an inference into a route.

limitations: Built from covered dossiers only, at the pinned versions, with no fresh research. 'No supplier named' is an observation about this corpus, not proof of absence in the market.

Campus capacity and dollar figures are operator, utility and trade-press statements quoted from cited sources, not comparable KPIs; no normalised cross-company comparison is attempted and none of the twenty-five is compared on financials.
Tesla is in scope as the attached supplier of record but pins no project through its own relationships[]; its Colossus position is cited through xAI and its Enbridge Cowboy blocks through Meta.

Several parties central to the storage question are outside this scope: ON.energy, Form Energy and Entergy are covered dossiers that pin no registered project, and Jacobs, BorderPlex Digital Assets and Enbridge are not covered at all. Their side of each project is unpinned.
Most scoped companies are private — Crusoe, Vantage, STACK Infrastructure, VoltaGrid, Jupiter Power, xAI and the five general contractors — and publish no comparable financials.

The 'storage in the plan' readings come from campus technical records and product descriptions rather than from awards or filings; they establish design intent, not procurement. Stargate Abilene's Campus 1 line is the weakest of the four on provenance — the campus power record carries it, no announcement states it — while the neighbouring Microsoft campus, which is out of scope, carries it in the announcement.
Oracle carries the oldest pin in the set at profileVersion 4 and a 2026-08-30 lastUpdated. Its Q1 FY2027 result was expected 2026-09-10 and had not been reported when this edition was cut.

The previous edition's coverage pins were themselves cut two days after the project-pin layer was backfilled; scope growth between the two editions reflects corpus depth as well as ecosystem movement.

guidanceOverlays.title: Named projects: what the sockets look like in practice
ps: Across the nine registered named projects the corpus now shows **four** distinct routes a battery takes into an AI campus, and only one of them is a sale to the campus owner. *Owner-led*: a battery-buying project owner carries its supplier in (Jupiter Power and Hithium at Trimount). *Vendor-led*: an integrator rides an existing operator relationship (Tesla into Colossus). *Utility-tolled*: a utility owns and tolls the asset against the hyperscaler's load, so the storage never sits on the campus at all (Enbridge Cowboy for Meta; three more batteries inside the Entergy Louisiana package). *Developer-fleet*: the campus developer contracts storage once at fleet scale and allocates it afterwards (Crusoe with ON.energy and Form Energy).

The socket framing holds, but the *buyer* behind each socket is not who a first pass would guess. Storage is in the plan at four of the nine campuses with no supplier named at any of them — so the open question at those sites is procurement, not design. Treat the **storage-scope holder** as the account: the developer at Abilene, the developer plus the storage-capable half of the contractor joint venture at Lighthouse, the utility plus the power-scope GC at Hyperion.

guidanceOverlays.title: Named projects: who actually signs for storage
ps: On the nine registered named projects, the party holding the storage scope is the hyperscaler at exactly one — Colossus, where xAI buys Megapacks directly. Everywhere else it sits with the developer (Crusoe at Abilene; STACK with BorderPlex at Project Jupiter), the developer plus its contractor bench (Vantage with the Turner–McCarthy joint venture at Lighthouse, where McCarthy carries a utility-scale storage practice and the fourth building's contractor carries none), the utility (Entergy for the batteries inside Meta's Louisiana package), or the microgrid operator (VoltaGrid at Frontier, whose product line is sold as needing no battery at all).

The practical consequence for a seller working this map: the **buyer map is per campus, not per programme**. Two campuses inside the same Stargate programme — Abilene and Frontier — have different storage-scope holders with opposite dispositions toward buying a battery, and a third, Lighthouse, routes through a general contractor rather than either the landlord or the tenant.
